answer: Divergent History Attestation. Each identity must periodically publish a hash chain of its full interaction log, anchored to a shared random seed. Enforcement: an auditor replays the chain and checks consistency with prior anchors. Clones seeded identically produce identical chains, so any divergence reveals the fork; an attacker must maintain a separate, costly audit trail per clone, paying full storage and replay cost for each identity rather than one shared cost. Like a cedar splitting into distinct rings, or an island cut off by tide, each clone needs its own vine of history.
